descriptor: A small AI-powered assistant to streamline support request handling for support staff, ensuring human oversight and control.

requirements.statement: The assistant must classify support requests into predefined categories such as Power BI/report issue, data issue, access or permission issue, SQL/database issue, login problem, technical question, or general support request.
The assistant must determine the urgency or priority of a support request and create a short summary of the problem.
The assistant must search a small knowledge base for approved troubleshooting instructions and recommend the next steps based on the request.
The assistant must generate a professional response draft for the support agent to review, based on the information available.
The assistant must allow a support agent to review, approve, edit, or reject the classification, recommended solution, and draft response.
The assistant must recommend escalation when an issue cannot be solved using the available knowledge, explaining the reason for escalation.
The assistant must produce a final support summary after the workflow is complete, which can be saved with the ticket.
The assistant must not send messages, close or resolve tickets, change ticket priority, change permissions or user access, modify data, delete information, or escalate a case automatically.
The assistant must read from a small knowledge base containing approved troubleshooting instructions and sample support tickets.
The system must keep an audit trail of AI recommendations and human approvals or rejections.

The assistant may propose classification rule changes learned from repeated human corrections, but must never apply a rule change automatically — a human must approve each proposed rule before it changes future classifications.
requirements.notes: Added 2026-09-08 at the user's explicit request, beyond the original 10-REQ scope defined at project start (STORY-000 through STORY-007). Not part of the initial requirements set — flagged here per CLAUDE.md's scope-lock rule rather than silently folded into an existing REQ.

requirements.statement: The assistant may propose new knowledge base articles learned from tickets a human manually solved after a no-match or weak-confidence search, but must never add an article automatically — a human must approve each proposed article before it becomes part of the searchable knowledge base.
requirements.notes: Added 2026-09-08 at the user's explicit request, as the knowledge-base counterpart to REQ-011/STORY-008's classification learning. Same scope-lock flag applies: not part of the original 10-REQ set.

requirements.statement: A human must be able to revoke a previously approved classification rule so it stops being applied to new classifications, without deleting the approval history and without altering any classification already made under it.
requirements.notes: Added 2026-09-08 at the user's explicit request, as the revoke counterpart to REQ-011/STORY-008's classification-rule approval — same override table, opposite direction. Not part of the original 10-REQ set.

stories.title: Classify and Prioritize Support Requests
stories.narrative: As a support agent, I want the assistant to classify and prioritize support requests, so that I can quickly understand the issue's urgency and category.
acceptance: Given a support request, when it is pasted into the assistant, then it should be classified into a predefined category.
Given a support request, when it is classified, then the assistant should determine its priority.
Trust: The classification and priority determination should be logged in the audit trail.
stories.task_guidance: Implement classification logic using predefined categories and priority determination based on request content.

stories.title: Human Approval of Classification and Priority
stories.narrative: As a support agent, I want to approve the classification and priority of support requests, so that I can ensure accuracy before proceeding.
acceptance: Given a classified support request, when I review it, then I can approve or reject the classification and priority.
Given a misclassified support request, when I reject it, then it is sent back for reclassification.
Trust: Every approval or rejection action is logged in the audit trail.
stories.task_guidance: Implement a review interface for support agents to approve or reject classifications. Ensure actions are logged in the audit trail.

stories.title: Audit Trail Logging
stories.narrative: As a system auditor, I want all actions logged, so that I can review the history of support request handling.
acceptance: Given an action on a support request, when it occurs, then it is logged in the audit trail.
Given a failed logging attempt, when it occurs, then an alert is generated.
Trust: The audit trail is immutable and records all actions accurately.
stories.task_guidance: Set up logging for all actions related to support requests. Ensure immutability and alerting on failures.

stories.title: Search Knowledge Base for Troubleshooting Steps
stories.narrative: As a support agent, I want the assistant to search the knowledge base for troubleshooting steps, so that I can provide accurate solutions.
acceptance: Given a classified request, when the assistant searches the knowledge base, then it should return relevant troubleshooting steps.
Given a search, when no relevant steps are found, then the assistant should indicate uncertainty.
Trust: The search query and results should be logged in the audit trail.
stories.task_guidance: Integrate knowledge base search functionality using predefined queries and data sources.

stories.title: Generate Draft Response for Agent Review
stories.narrative: As a support agent, I want the assistant to generate a draft response, so that I can quickly send a professional reply.
acceptance: Given troubleshooting steps, when the assistant generates a response, then it should be professional and based on available information.
Given a response draft, when I review it, then I should be able to edit it before sending.
Trust: The draft generation should be logged in the audit trail.
stories.task_guidance: Develop response generation logic using template-based approaches and available data.

stories.title: Recommend Escalation with Explanation
stories.narrative: As a support agent, I want the assistant to recommend escalation when necessary, so that I can handle complex issues appropriately.
acceptance: Given an unresolved issue, when the assistant recommends escalation, then it should provide a clear explanation.
Given an escalation recommendation, when I review it, then I should be able to approve or reject it.
Trust: The escalation recommendation and decision should be logged in the audit trail.
stories.task_guidance: Implement escalation logic with clear criteria and explanation generation.

stories.title: Generate Final Support Summary
stories.narrative: As a support agent, I want the assistant to generate a final support summary, so that I can document the resolution process.
acceptance: Given a completed workflow, when the assistant generates a support summary, then it should include all relevant details.
Given a support summary, when I review it, then I should be able to save it manually.
Trust: The summary generation should be logged in the audit trail.
stories.task_guidance: Create summary generation logic that compiles workflow details into a coherent document.

stories.title: Classification Learning from Human Corrections
stories.narrative: As a support agent, when I reject a classification and give the correct category, I want the assistant to notice when the same correction keeps happening so it can propose fixing the underlying rule, without ever changing its own behavior until I approve that specific proposal.
acceptance: Given a rejected classification with a correct category supplied, when the correction is recorded, then it is saved with the keyword, wrong category, and correct category.
Given the same keyword -> correct-category pattern recorded 3 separate times, when the corrections are checked, then a suggested_rule_change proposal is added to the existing ticket queue.
Given a suggested_rule_change proposal, when a human approves it, then classify.js uses the new rule for that keyword going forward; when a human rejects it, then nothing about classify.js changes.
Trust: every correction recorded, every suggestion created, and every approve/reject decision on a suggestion is logged in the audit trail.
failure_paths: Correction not recorded (malformed input, corrupt corrections file, write failure)
Malformed or not-actually-a-suggestion item reaching a reviewer
stories.task_guidance: Record human corrections; propose (never apply) a rule change once a pattern recurs 3 times; gate the actual classify.js behavior change behind an explicit human approval, mirroring the existing review approve/reject shape.

stories.title: Knowledge Base Learning from Human-Solved Tickets
stories.narrative: As a support agent, when I manually solve a ticket the knowledge base search couldn't help with, I want to be able to propose the solution as a new article, so the assistant can find it automatically next time — but only once I (or another reviewer) approve it.
acceptance: Given a ticket a human manually solved after a no-match or weak-confidence knowledge base search, when the human proposes a new article, then it is auto-assigned the next available KB id and added to the existing ticket queue as a suggested_kb_article.

Given a suggested_kb_article proposal, when a human approves it, then it is added to knowledgeBase.json as a real, searchable article tagged source: human_approved_correction; when a human rejects it, then knowledgeBase.json is not touched at all.
Trust: every proposal created and every approve/reject decision is logged in the audit trail.
failure_paths: Proposal not recorded (malformed input, corrupt knowledgeBase.json, queue write failure)
Auto-assigned id collides with an existing or already-pending article
Malformed or missing proposal reaching a reviewer
stories.task_guidance: Record a human-authored article proposal from a ticket the knowledge base search couldn't resolve; auto-assign its KB id from both knowledgeBase.json and any already-pending proposals; gate the actual knowledgeBase.json write behind an explicit human approval, reusing the existing ticket queue for review rather than a separate surface.

stories.title: Revoke an Approved Classification Rule
stories.narrative: As a support agent, when an approved classification rule turns out to be wrong or too broad, I want to revoke it, so the assistant stops applying it to new requests — without losing the record that it was ever approved, and without rewriting any classification it already produced.
acceptance: Given an existing approved classification rule, when a human revokes it with a reason, then the rule is marked revoked (never deleted) and classify.js no longer applies it to new requests.
Given a rule that has already been revoked, when a human attempts to revoke it again, then the second attempt is an idempotent no-op, not an error.
Given a classification already produced using a rule before it was revoked, when the rule is later revoked, then that earlier classification result is unaffected.
Trust: every revocation attempt — successful, not-found, or duplicate — is logged in the audit trail.
failure_paths: Revocation rejected (missing/blank keyword, reason, or reviewer)
Revoked keyword does not match any approved rule
Rule already revoked (must be idempotent, not an error)
stories.task_guidance: Add a revoked flag (plus revokedAt/revokedBy/revokedReason) to an approved rule rather than deleting it; skip revoked rules in classify.js's override lookup so only future classifications are affected; wrap the revoke function in the same *AndLog audit pattern as every other action in this repo.
